questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE about the right to freedom of religion mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: It provides freedom to manage religious affairs.
questions.option_3: It mentions that the state has its own religion.
questions.option_4: It is mentioned in Articles 25 to 28.
questions.solution: The statement that 'the state has its own religion' is FALSE. India is a secular state, meaning it does not uphold any particular religion as the official state religion. Articles 25 to 28 guarantee freedom of conscience, the right to profess, practice, and propagate religion, and the freedom to manage religious affairs. Note: The Indian concept of secularism implies 'Sarva Dharma Sambhava' (equal respect for all religions).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution directs the state to provide for a “Uniform Civil Code’?
questions.solution: Article 44 (DPSP) directs the State to endeavor to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout the territory of India. This aims to replace personal laws based on scriptures and customs of each major religious community with a common set of laws governing every citizen. Current Status: While it remains a directive, Goa is currently the only Indian state with a functional UCC.

questions.question: Which of the following are categorized in the Right to Constitutional Remedies in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is primarily centered on Article 32, but the broader category in the constitutional structure (Part III) ends with Articles 32-35. These articles provide the machinery for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, including the power of Parliament to modify these rights for the armed forces (Art 33) and the power to legislate to give effect to Part III (Art 35).

questions.question: Article 51 A of the Indian Constitution came into effect from ________.
questions.solution: Article 51A (Fundamental Duties) came into effect on 31st January 1977. It was introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 during the Internal Emergency. Fact: Initially, 10 duties were added; the 11th was added much later in 2002.

questions.question: The government scheme, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, aims for crop insurance service for farmers. This type of government effort falls under _______ of theDirective Principle of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana aligns with Article 48, which directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines. By providing insurance, the state helps modernize the risk-management aspect of farming. Related: Article 48 also mentions the preservation and improvement of breeds.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void?
questions.solution: Article 13 is a powerful provision that acts as a protector of Fundamental Rights. It declares that all laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights shall be void. This article effectively establishes the doctrine of Judicial Review in India, empowering the courts to strike down unconstitutional legislation.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the right to form co-operative societies?
questions.solution: The right to form co-operative societies is a Fundamental Right mentioned under Article 19(1)(c). This specific inclusion was made by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011. Note: The same amendment also added a Directive Principle (Art 43B) and a new Part IX-B to the Constitution.

questions.question: Since complete equality is impossible, the equal protection of the Indian Constitution is subject to proper classification.
questions.solution: Article 14 guarantees both 'Equality before the Law' and 'Equal Protection of the Laws'. The latter implies that among equals, the law should be equal and equally administered. This allows the state to make reasonable classifications (e.g., special laws for women or children) as long as they are not arbitrary.

questions.question: A father was speaking about the rich cultural heritage of India to his young son and his teenager friends. The fundamental duty in which Article was the father promoting?
questions.solution: The father was promoting the fundamental duty mentioned in Article 51A(f), which is 'to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture'. Context: India’s culture is described as 'composite' because it is a blend of various traditions, languages, and religions that have evolved together over centuries.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned in Article 39 A of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: To secure adequate means of livelihood
questions.option_2: To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid
questions.solution: Article 39A (added by the 42nd Amendment) mandates the State to promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to the poor and vulnerable. This ensures that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. Legal Impact: This article led to the establishment of NALSA and Lok Adalats.

questions.question: Under which of the following Articles of the Indian constitution "Equality of opportunities include its reasonable classification and provisions for backward class of citizens" is provided?
questions.solution: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. However, it also allows for reasonable classification and enables the State to make provisions for the reservation of appointments or posts in favor of any backward class of citizens which is not adequately represented in the services.

questions.question: The Fundamental Rights have been guaranteed to protect the public from repressive state actions: judicial decisions tend to expand the scope of the word 'State' as defined by __________ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution: Article 12 provides the definition of 'the State' for the purpose of Fundamental Rights. It includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities. Expansion: Judicial decisions have expanded this to include statutory and non-statutory bodies like LIC, ONGC, and even some private bodies performing public functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is enforceable by the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Among the options, only Fundamental Rights are enforceable (justiciable) by the courts. If they are violated, a person can approach the High Court (Art 226) or Supreme Court (Art 32) directly. Contrast: The Preamble, DPSPs, and Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning you cannot sue the government for not fulfilling them.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_2: They can be suspended during emergency
questions.solution: The feature 'They are negative in nature' is actually a characteristic of several Fundamental Rights (which restrict the state), but Fundamental Duties are generally positive in nature (as they urge citizens to do something). Correction: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, and while they aren't 'available against the state' like rights, they serve as a warning against anti-social activities.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution is FALSE?
questions.option_1: They provide necessary conditions for material protection.
questions.option_2: They provide necessary conditions for moral protection.
questions.option_3: They provide necessary conditions for practicing untouchability.
questions.option_4: They lay down the foundation for social justice.
questions.solution: The statement that Fundamental Rights 'provide necessary conditions for practicing untouchability' is FALSE. On the contrary, Article 17 specifically abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice. Fundamental Rights are designed to provide moral and material protection and serve as the bedrock of social justice.

questions.question: Which of the following committees had recommended incorporating the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the incorporation of Fundamental Duties into the Constitution. Interestingly, the committee suggested 8 duties, but the 42nd Amendment incorporated 10. Note: The committee also suggested making these duties enforceable with penalties, but that part was not accepted.

questions.question: When were the Fundamental Duties first added in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Fundamental Duties were first added to the Indian Constitution in 1976 via the 42nd Amendment. This occurred during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi. Note: This part of the constitution was heavily inspired by the Constitution of the USSR.

questions.question: The committee to operationalize the Suggestions to Teach Fundamental Duties to the Citizens of the Country’ is popularly known as the _________.
questions.solution: The J.S. Verma Committee (1999) was appointed to operationalize the suggestions to teach Fundamental Duties to the citizens. It identified the existence of legal provisions for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties (like the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_2: To uphold and protect the country's sovereignty
questions.option_3: To promote harmony and the spirit of brotherhood
questions.solution: To protect monuments is NOT a Fundamental Duty of the citizen under Article 51A; it is a Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 49) for the State. Clarification: While citizens have a duty to preserve 'rich heritage' (51A-f), the specific obligation to protect and maintain monuments rests with the government.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_2: They are not sacrosanct or permanent.
questions.option_3: There is a legal sanction against their violation.
questions.option_4: They are part of the Indian tradition.
questions.solution: The statement that 'there is a legal sanction against their violation' is NOT a feature of Fundamental Duties. They are non-justiciable, meaning the Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement by courts. Note: However, Parliament can enact separate laws (like the Wildlife Protection Act) to punish actions that violate the spirit of these duties.

questions.question: Which of the following Provisions of the Indian Constitution is taken from the US Constitution?
questions.option_1: Procedure for amendment of the constitution
questions.solution: The post of Vice President and the concept of Fundamental Rights were taken from the US Constitution. Other sources: Amendment procedure is from South Africa, Fundamental Duties from the USSR, and Bicameralism from Britain.

questions.question: What is the aim of fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The primary aim of Fundamental Rights is to establish political democracy. They prevent the establishment of an authoritarian or dictatorial rule and protect the liberties of the people against the invasion by the State. Contrast: Directive Principles aim to establish social and economic democracy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_2: To develop the spirit of inquiry
questions.option_4: To develop the spirit of harmony
questions.solution: To bring reform is NOT a specifically listed Fundamental Duty in Article 51A. Included Duties: To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform (Art 51A-h). While 'reform' is mentioned within that clause, 'to bring reform' as a standalone duty is not specified.

questions.question: In India, which of the following statements is NOT correct about Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution: 'To organize village panchayat' is NOT a Fundamental Duty; it is a Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 40). Included Duties: Protecting the country, encouraging brotherhood, and developing scientific temper are all valid Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities was appointed as the legal advisor of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution?
questions.solution: Sir B.N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly. He was responsible for preparing the initial draft of the Constitution. Note: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, and S.N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draftsman.

questions.question: Which of the following words was NOT a part of the original Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The word 'Secular' was NOT in the original Preamble of 1950. It was added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, along with 'Socialist' and 'Integrity'. The original Preamble described India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'.

questions.question: The Political Part of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from which Constitution?
questions.solution: The Political Part of the Indian Constitution (dealing with the executive and the legislature) is largely drawn from the British Constitution. This includes the Cabinet system, the Parliamentary form of government, and the rule of law. Note: This is why India follows a Westminster model of government.
